extracted.intended_audience: Doctoral students, dissertation-stage candidates, and early-career scholars applying for Ford Foundation fellowships (predoctoral, dissertation, postdoctoral, and Ford Global applicants).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for applicants to Ford Foundation fellowships (predoctoral, dissertation, postdoctoral) and the Ford Global Fellowship; focuses on academic merit, commitment to academic careers, and demonstrated use of diversity as an educational resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase ethnic and racial diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Program purpose: Designed to increase ethnic and racial diversity of the nation's college and university faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core program goal that informs selection; applicants should demonstrate how their candidacy or future work would contribute to increasing ethnic and racial diversity in higher education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizing the educational benefits of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Program purpose: Maximize the educational benefits of diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to show how their perspectives, experiences, or approaches will enhance classroom learning and intellectual environment for a diverse student body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase number of professors who use diversity as an educational resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Program purpose: Increase the number of professors who use diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates likely to integrate diverse perspectives into teaching and scholarship so that diversity itself becomes an instructional asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior academic achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criterion: Candidates must demonstrate superior academic achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators will look for evidence of high scholarly performance (transcripts, publications, letters) indicating readiness for an academic career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to a career in teaching and research at the college or university level
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criterion: Demonstrated commitment to an academic career combining teaching and research at higher-education institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should articulate long-term career plans, prior teaching or research experience, and motivation for pursuing a faculty role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criterion: Promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors judge potential for future scholarly productivity and effective teaching (e.g., research agenda, letters of recommendation, dissertation progress).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criterion (reiterated): Evidence that the applicant will use diversity as a resource to enrich student education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete plans or past examples of integrating diverse perspectives into curricula, pedagogy, or scholarship that benefit all students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to respond pedagogically to diverse student learning needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evaluation factor: Capacity to respond in pedagogically productive ways to the learning needs of students from diverse backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide examples of pedagogical strategies, teaching experience, or training that demonstrate responsiveness to varied cultural, linguistic, and educational backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained personal engagement with underrepresented communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evaluation factor: Sustained personal engagement with communities that are underrepresented in the academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators value long-term community involvement (service, outreach, mentoring) that reflects genuine commitment rather than one-off activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of using diversity of human experience in teaching and scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evaluation factor: Likelihood of using the diversity of human experience as an educational resource in teaching and scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should show plans or a record of research/teaching that draws on diverse human experiences to advance knowledge and pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership in severely underrepresented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evaluation/consideration: Membership in one or more groups whose underrepresentation in the American professoriate has been severe and longstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a member of such groups is a factor considered in selection; applicants should indicate and, where appropriate, contextualize their membership and its relevance to the program's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ford Global Fellowship: diverse approaches to disrupting inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Global criterion: Wide diversity of approaches and ways of thinking about disrupting inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should present novel, varied, or interdisciplinary approaches to addressing inequality at global or transnational scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ford Global Fellowship: demonstrated meaningful impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Global criterion: Diverse array of committed leaders who have demonstrated meaningful impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors leaders with documented impact (programs, policy changes, community outcomes) rather than solely theoretical engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ford Global Fellowship: potential limited by lack of resources/access
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Global criterion: Candidates whose full potential has yet to be fully realized due to lack of resources or access to a global network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for applicants who would substantially benefit from funding and networking to scale or realize their work's potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ford Global Fellowship: focus on root causes of inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Global criterion: People examining and addressing the root causes of inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate work that interrogates and targets structural or systemic drivers of inequality, not only symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible disciplines and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility constraint: Includes humanities, behavioral and social sciences, sciences, engineering, mathematics, computer science; excludes professional degree programs (MBA, JD, MD, etc.) and creative writing/arts MFAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in eligible academic disciplines; applicants enrolled in excluded professional or creative-practice degrees are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship types and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Program detail: Three types — Predoctoral (3 years support for students entering or in early years of research-based PhD/ScD), Dissertation (1 year support to complete dissertation), Postdoctoral (1 year support for early-career scholars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should apply to the fellowship type matching their career stage; duration and purpose vary by type and affect eligibility and expectations.
